walkthrough.title: Get started with Dead CSS Cleaner
walkthrough.description: Find CSS selectors that nothing in your project uses, understand why each one was flagged, and remove them safely.
walkthrough.analyze.title: Run your first analysis
walkthrough.analyze.description:
Run **Dead CSS Cleaner: Analyze Workspace for Dead CSS** from the Command Palette, click the status bar item, or press `Ctrl+Alt+D`.

Existing dead selectors are also found automatically whenever you save a file.
walkthrough.review.title: Review the findings
walkthrough.review.description:
Dead selectors appear in the **Problems** panel with the exact class or id underlined, and in the **Dead CSS by component** view in the activity bar.

Hover a finding to see why it was flagged, whether the selector is only *partially* dead, and which files were checked - including the child components that may use a parent's stylesheet.
walkthrough.fix.title: Fix them in one click
walkthrough.fix.description:
Open the lightbulb menu on a finding to **remove the token**, **remove the whole rule**, or **add an ignore comment**.

You can also run **Remove All Dead Selectors in This File** for a bulk cleanup.
walkthrough.tune.title: Tune it to your project
walkthrough.tune.description:
If a dynamically built class is reported wrongly, add a prefix to `unusedCssDetector.dynamicClassPatterns` or `unusedCssDetector.safelist`, or mark the rule with `/* dead-css-ignore */`.

Switch `unusedCssDetector.analysisMode` to `strict` for quieter, fully-dead-only reporting.
